analysis:
This batch contains only offline CI test files. They describe a release-routing change but do not include its implementation: resolve-provider-release.sh, provider_release_resume/api.py, release-provider.yml and release-dev-branch.yml are not supplied.

Asserted head behavior:
- scripts/test-provider-release-resolution.py:43-55: a dispatched dev lane resolves only as an unpublished validation build. A dev publication without a dev push fails.
- Same file, 57-77: a master push publishes staging only. A master push routed to dev, prod or nothing fails.
- Same file, 79-106: a dev push publishes dev only as 0.9.0-dev.branch.N. Other refs, including devx and dev/x, are refused.
- Same file, 156: staging tags are refused.
- scripts/test-provider-release-resume.py:135-173: verify_workflow_source accepts a dev push only for RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=dev. The commit must be GitHub-verified and on dev-branch ancestry. Dev ancestry cannot satisfy a master route.

The tests tighten routing. They do not show any prod path that loosened.

Material unverified change: the scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py head docstring (file_changes patch, head 2-19) says the dev-branch lane changed. It is now a push-to-dev caller of the reusable release-provider.yml with secrets: inherit. That workflow signs with the Apple Developer ID and notarizes. Previously the lane was dispatch-only, self-signed and barred from the production Apple signing identity. The dev branch now becomes a source of Developer-ID-signed, notarized provider binaries.

Relevant threat IDs: T-013, T-034, T-054, A-011 and A-017. Consumers must not treat Developer ID team signing or notarization as official-build qualification. The canonical model says qualification is an independently approved full CodeDirectory identity, which should hold, but backend policy is platform-owned and outside this evidence.

Open questions for integration:
- Is the dev branch protected, i.e. are reviewed and verified commits enforced? Ancestry plus GitHub verification is the only source gate the tests show.
- Does secrets: inherit expose only DEV_* plus Apple signing secrets, with no PROD/STAGING keys, as the docstring claims?
- Can a dev-signed binary register against prod or staging coordinators?

No cited lines are visible for the workflow, and unit b7ec82171e4e0025:0 is metadata-only, so I raised no finding.
